public_rationale: Research documents sycophancy, capability overconfidence and an earlier case where developers felt faster while actually taking longer. Those findings make parts of the claim plausible. They do not establish its broad description of LLMs in August 2026. METR's follow-up also cautions against carrying its earlier slowdown forward. The evidence does not justify either blanket support or blanket contradiction.
limitations: The universal wording and undefined value threshold materially affect interpretation.
Earlier or narrower studies are context, not decisive target-period evidence.
Useful output cannot be reduced to completion speed alone.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: LLMs, built to respond with the most likely desired output, tell every user their every idea is genius, promise to help with just about anything even when incapable of it, and can make users feel very productive while creating only the appearance of productivity without producing very much value.

statement.excerpt: As a technology built to respond with what is most likely to be the desired output, they tell every user their every idea is genius, promise to help out with just about anything (even if they’re incapable of doing so), and are capable of making you feel really productive as you endlessly prompt an ever-growing system

from_speaker: tell every user their every idea is genius
promise to help out with just about anything
even if they’re incapable of doing so
capable of making you feel really productive
our_interpretation: I read the universal language as an emphatic claim about common behavior, rather than a claim that no contrary interaction exists.
The productivity clause describes a possible mismatch between perceived productivity and useful output. It does not say that every use of an LLM lacks value.
Useful output means completed work of adequate quality, accounting for time spent prompting, checking and correcting.

The post describes an ongoing state without dates. I use August 2026, the last complete month before publication, as the target period. Earlier experiments provide context, not direct measurements of that period.
criteria.support_condition: Representative interaction audits show widespread unwarranted praise and commitments beyond demonstrated capabilities, and controlled workflows demonstrate that users can feel more productive while producing little additional useful work.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative audits contradict the claimed general pattern of flattery or overpromising. For the productivity component, matched measurements must address the described workflows; gains in unrelated tasks do not disprove the possibility of illusory productivity.

evidence.explanation: The study documents models abandoning correct medical answers under pressure, with substantial variation by interaction design. Medical agreement is narrower than praising every idea, and the abstract does not date the trials precisely enough to establish August behavior.

In the February–June 2025 experiment, developers believed AI saved time although measured completion time increased. This establishes an earlier perception gap, but does not measure August 2026 models or all dimensions of value.

The follow-up experiment began in August 2025 and pointed toward speedups. METR warns that selection effects make the estimates unreliable, so neither its earlier slowdown nor these later estimates settle the broad current claim.

evidence.excerpt: All LLMs we tested are overconfident
evidence.publisher: arXiv; Casey O. Barkan, Sid Black and Oliver Sourbut
evidence.explanation: The research supports concern about capability overconfidence while also finding some ability to distinguish likely success from failure. It measures earlier systems' confidence, rather than the prevalence of promises made to users in August 2026.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Target-period interaction audits and controlled workflow studies measuring praise, promises, perceived productivity, completed work and correction costs across representative models and users.
